reasons: The docstrings refer to a test that blocks money fields, but that test is not in this packet, so it is unverified.
The sharing check uses only the high ends of ranges, which may be looser than the author intended.
No error handling for the value engine is visible here, since it lives in another package.

terms.meaning: A low and a high estimate, used to show uncertainty instead of a single number.
The amount of human work consumed, measured in full-time equivalents. Shares are measured against this.
Full-time equivalent: one person working full time for a year, used as a unit of effort.
A shared capability that several processes depend on, counted once so its value is not added twice.
Something that must be finished before this process can be delivered.
How many months it takes for people to fully start using the change.

depends_on: packages/value/ (named in the docstring as the place for all arithmetic)
used_by: packages/value/ (the value engine, named in the docstring)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and no-money rule
sections.what: Explains that this object holds only estimates about effort and shares, with no currency or total of any kind, and that the calculations belong to a separate value package.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: an agent estimates, and the arithmetic has one exact answer that code should compute.
sections.watch_out: Do not add money or total fields here. The docstring says such figures belong in the value package.

sections.name: Prerequisite
sections.title: Prerequisite dependency entry
sections.what: Defines one thing that must land before a process can be delivered, with its kind, a reference, a reason and the evidence behind it.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: most real prerequisites are not processes, so a process-only link would schedule work that cannot start. Shared value is kept separate.
sections.watch_out: Do not use this entry to express shared value. That is the job of the shared enabler list.

sections.name: ValueParameters (part 1)
sections.title: Effort and share estimates
sections.what: Holds the estimated effort used today, the share that could be fully automated, the share that stays human but is assisted, the efficiency gain within the assisted share, the time compression, the error rate, the adoption ramp and the shared enabler list.
sections.why: Each value is a range so uncertainty stays visible. The docstring says the efficiency gain is its own field so the engine does not assume a hidden constant.
sections.watch_out: Shares are fractions of effort, not step counts or elapsed time. The time compression field is elapsed time and must not be multiplied by effort.

sections.name: ValueParameters (part 2)
sections.title: Dependencies, evidence and share check
sections.what: Holds the list of prerequisites and the evidence ids. It also includes a check that the high ends of the automatable and assisted shares together do not exceed the whole.
sections.why: Stated in the code: work cannot be more than fully covered.
sections.watch_out: The check reads only the high ends of the ranges, so the low ends are not tested against the total.

summary: Defines the estimated inputs for a process's value, meaning effort, shares of work that can be automated or assisted, and dependencies, but never any money amounts.
purpose: Hold the only numbers an agent may estimate about a process's worth, so the arithmetic that turns them into money is done in one place by code.
why: The docstrings say an agent estimates under uncertainty, which is what a model is for, while exact multiplication and totals belong to code.
how: 1) The file states the rule that no money field exists here. 2) The Prerequisite class describes one dependency with its kind, reference, reason and evidence. 3) The ValueParameters class lists effort, automation and assistance shares, efficiency gain, time compression, error rate, adoption ramp, shared enabler ids, dependencies and evidence. 4) A check confirms automatable and assisted shares at their high ends do not add to more than one.
inputs: Estimates produced by an agent for one process, each as a range with bounds.
outputs: A validated, frozen ValueParameters object used by the value engine and the record. A rejected object raises an error naming the numbers that broke the rule.
risks: A field added here that carries money would bypass the value engine. The sharing check compares only the high ends of the ranges. Shares must be fractions of effort, not steps or elapsed time, and the docstrings say mixing these double-counts savings.
debug: If parameters are rejected, read the error for the two share values and their sum. Check that shares are fractions of effort. If a total looks inflated, check that shared enabler ids are from the closed list, since free text never matches and the total is not deduplicated.
